content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Summarise the key concepts of respiration
Link respiration to other body systems
Review key equations, terms, and experimental methods

This lesson brings together all the key concepts of respiration. Respiration is central to biology - it's how all living cells release energy from glucose. Understanding respiration helps explain exercise, metabolism, and how organisms survive in different conditions.
Provides energy for ALL life processes
Links to nutrition, transport, and excretion
Fast: Restore PC and O₂ stores (2-3 min)
Slow: Remove lactic acid (up to 1 hour)
Outer membrane, inner membrane, cristae, matrix
Organism, soda lime, coloured liquid, capillary tube
Oxygen deficit, steady state, oxygen debt
Respiration is cellular; breathing is ventilation
Lactic acid causes days of soreness
Chemical reactions releasing energy from glucose
Product of anaerobic respiration in animals
Respiration releases energy from glucose in all living cells
Aerobic: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + ATP (~36-38)
Anaerobic: glucose → lactic acid OR ethanol + CO₂ + ATP (~2)
ATP is the universal energy currency
Mitochondria are the main site (aerobic); cytoplasm (anaerobic)
Exercise increases respiration; intense exercise triggers anaerobic
Oxygen debt = extra oxygen needed after exercise for recovery
RQ indicates which substrate is being respired
Respiration links to nutrition, transport, excretion, and homeostasis
